sources: Evans-Wentz, W. Y. The Fairy-Faith in Celtic Countries. Gerrards Cross: Colin Smythe Humanities Press, 1911, 79.
Monaghan, Patricia. The Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore. Checkmark Books, 2008.
text: Geróid Iarla, also known as Gerald, Earl of Desmond, and the Red Earl, is an Irish hero. The Earl Maurice saw the fairy queen Áine swimming as a swan at the mouth of the River Comóg into Lough Gur. He stole her cloak, and she bore their child Geróid. Áine set one condition: Maurice must show no astonishment at anything his son did. At a banquet Geróid leaped into a bottle and out again. Maurice showed surprise. The boy and his mother vanished into the lake, or Geróid became the goose that swam by. Every seven years Geróid rides from Lough Gur on a white horse.

okr.objective: Document Geróid Iarla as an Irish hero of fairy descent from Lough Gur.
